<thought>After analyzing the mass (M≈100 Da → C₅H₈O₂), the ¹³C NMR (five distinct carbons, two sp² at ~136/117 ppm, one O‑bearing at ~70 ppm, two sp³ at ~54/44 ppm), and the ¹H NMR (methyl 3H at 2.93 ppm coupled to a methine at 4.43 ppm; a terminal alkene CH₂ at 5.04 ppm (J ≈ 16.7 Hz) and a vinylic CH at 6.05 ppm coupled trans to the CH₂ and also to the methine), the structure that fits all data is a molecule containing a terminal alkene attached to a carbon bearing both a hydroxyl and a methyl group, plus an additional oxygen as an ether. The structure that satisfies the formula C₅H₈O₂ and the NMR pattern is **3‑methoxy‑1‑buten‑2‑ol**, whose SMILES representation is `CC(O)C=CO`. This SMILES yields the correct molecular formula, carbon count, and the observed coupling relationships.** 

<final_answer>CC(O)C=CO</final_answer>
